chunks: Ḥammād narrated from al-Ḥalabī, who said:
I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who bought a garment and then returned it to its owner, but he refused to rescind the sale except with a reduction.

He عليه السلام said: “It is not proper for him to take it back with a reduction. If he was unaware and took it back, then sold it for more than its price, he must return the excess to the first owner.”

key_terms.بِوَضِيعَةٍ: with a reduction in price or loss deduction
key_terms.ثَوْبًا: a garment being bought and returned in the transaction
key_terms.مَا زَادَ: the extra amount gained above the original price
key_terms.يُقِيلَهُ: to rescind or cancel the sale

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to take back a returned sold item from the seller at a reduced price and keep the later profit?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on rescinding a sale with a price reduction after a garment has been returned to the seller. The Imam عليه السلام states that such an arrangement is not valid for the buyer, and if it occurs out of ignorance and leads to profit, the extra amount belongs to the original seller.
